solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Occupying bedsit, bloke activated blow-up doll?

definitions.note: describes the state of the doll rather than naming it, hence the question mark

parts.note: occupying a place is being in it
a bedsit is a small one-room flat
a man's name standing for any bloke

explanation.surface: A lonely man in his bedsit gets his blow-up doll ready.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat. The definition is descriptive: a blow-up doll that has been activated has been pumped full of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing air into a doll swells it up, which is exactly the past-participle sense of being filled with air.

clue.text: The issue of a blustering politician's latest broadcast?

definitions.text: The issue of a blustering politician

parts.note: the latest news is hot off the press
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A sneer at the newest speech transmitted by a windbag MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks like a possessive tying 'latest' to the politician, but it is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, boastful talk is the idiomatic product of a blusterer, so it is what such a politician issues.

clue.text: Some debs screwed around, having a number of studs

indicators.note: something screwed around has been twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip about society girls sleeping around with a string of hunky studs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like it selects letters from 'debs', but both words are the anagram fodder. Debs are debutantes, upper-class girls entering society.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface decorated with raised studs or bosses is described as embossed.

clue.text: City big in clothing has star Jennifer jack off

indicators.note: with jack, the card J, taken off, that letter is removed from the star's nickname

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the label for large clothes
J.Lo is the nickname of the singer and actress Jennifer Lopez

explanation.surface: A city where a big star is undressing, with a smutty pun at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack off' reads as vulgar slang, but jack is J, which is removed from J.Lo.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Union crushed by Iron Lady (mad, youth gone) — "A type of outmoded social system"

definitions.text: A type of outmoded social system

indicators.note: something crushed by two things is squeezed between them
mad letters are deranged, so they are put in a new order
the letter standing for youth goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
U is a standard abbreviation for union
taken as written, before its Y (youth) is dropped

explanation.surface: A jibe that Thatcher, the Iron Lady, crushed the unions and ran an antique social order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' is Thatcher's nickname, but the words are split: Iron gives FE and Lady loses Y (youth, as in YMCA) before LAD is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism is the medieval system of lords, vassals and serfs, long since abandoned.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Hoping to reduce girth of misshapen dong? Gate no. II

indicators.note: something misshapen has lost its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with II as two letters I

explanation.surface: A smutty scandal-name, Donggate, about a misshapen member.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Gate no. II' parodies scandal names like Watergate; it is just fodder, with the Roman numeral read as two I's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes on a diet is trying to lose weight and slim the waistline.

clue.text: Port combative sports types poured into Greek

indicators.note: something poured into a vessel ends up inside it

parts.note: Gk is the dictionary abbreviation for Greek
dans are grades of skill in judo and karate

explanation.surface: Fighters crowding into a Greek bar or port.
explanation.walkthrough: A dan is a black-belt rank in martial arts, so the 'types' are grades, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Baltic seaport in northern Poland.

clue.text: One name for Madonna's no.1: Snitch

parts.note: the Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation for name
taken as written

indicators.note: number one means the leading letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: Reads like a chart item about a Madonna number one single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madonna's no.1' suggests a hit record, but it means just her first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To snitch is to tell tales to the authorities, which is the verb's sense of passing on information.

clue.text: Drugs supplied by tosser I'd tossed

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym-goer admitting the drugs came from some jerk they had thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for a contemptible man; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are a class of drugs, notoriously taken by athletes and bodybuilders.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) Mature Fish's beer in barrelfuls? That'll give you balls

parts.note: things that come by the barrel come in a load
mature means grown old
the cod is a fish, with the S kept
wallop is old British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts that barrels of a brewer's mature ale will make a man of you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' looks like the courage that drink gives; it is the British slang sense of nonsense. Fish is also a brewer's name in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls and codswallop are both British slang for complete nonsense.

clue.text: Tip from Cameron bound to produce sod all?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: David Cameron was famously reported in 2011 for leaving no gratuity at an Italian café
second meaning: British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A dig that the Prime Minister's gratuity is sure to amount to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is topical: in 2011 newspapers mocked Cameron for not tipping a waitress in Tuscany. Sod all is coarse British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount Cameron left and the amount meant by sod all are both zero, the plain pronoun for not any.

clue.text: True, getting screwed by American, gives a person a start in life

definitions.text: gives a person a start in life
definitions.note: describes what the organ does rather than naming it

indicators.note: a thing screwed is twisted out of true, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A frank remark that a sexual encounter with an American can start a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the womb is where a person's life begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb is the organ in which a baby develops before birth, its earliest home.

clue.text: Cobblers toss back hair

indicators.note: back means the word for toss is read from right to left

parts.note: to lob is to toss something in a high arc
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: Shoemakers throwing hair back over their shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers looks like shoe-menders, but it is British rhyming slang (cobblers' awls, balls) meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for rubbish or nonsense, used as exclamations of disbelief.

clue.text: Doctor in bra whom Brenda makes wait

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor in a bra kept hanging about by some woman called Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames the Queen Brenda and Prince Charles Brian; she kept her heir waiting decades for the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Prince Charles, the heir the Queen kept waiting.

clue.text: Duke leading fanatical semi-military group might be a threat to Brown?

definitions.text: might be a threat to Brown

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
avid means keen to the point of fanaticism

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: the first four of its eight letters
a band is a group

explanation.surface: A duke heading an extremist militia sounds like a danger to someone named Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is Gordon Brown, Labour Prime Minister 2007-10, whose Foreign Secretary was talked of as a leadership rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour politician was widely tipped as a possible challenger to Gordon Brown's leadership.

clue.text: Wood's first old queen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name of the comedian ... Wood
second meaning: Britain's monarch of 1837 to 1901

explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Wood was a much-loved British comedian and writer; 'first' means her first name, not a first letter. 'Old queen' also hints at the slang for an aging gay man.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the comic matches the name of the long-reigning nineteenth-century British monarch.

clue.text: One needs one to embrace New Labour — hardly cool

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation for new
a means one, as in a single item
to sweat is to toil or labour

explanation.surface: A political line: one has to warm to New Labour, which is hardly cool.
explanation.walkthrough: New Labour was Tony Blair's rebranded party, but here New is N and Labour is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sweating is overheated or anxious, the opposite of keeping cool.

clue.text: Imperious unnatural ability needed to interrupt party jerk

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another word

parts.note: a do is a party
extrasensory perception, a supernatural power
a tic is a twitch or involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A haughty psychic barging into a party to deal with some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerk looks like an insult, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot rules absolutely, so despotic behaviour is overbearing and imperious.

clue.text: Woman's lover has decorated, medium one

parts.note: fancy means ornamented
M is the clothing size for medium
an means one

explanation.surface: A woman's boyfriend has done up the place, or perhaps one has visited a medium.
explanation.walkthrough: Fancy man is a dated British term for a woman's lover, usually illicit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy man is a dated colloquial term for a woman's boyfriend or paramour.

clue.text: Rude brat tossed without having an erection

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
things tossed are thrown about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a man with an erection is said to be up

explanation.surface: A rude spoiled child thrown out without any sign of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without having' looks like 'lacking', but without means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt manner is curt and brusque, a common sense of rude.

clue.text: Excrement all over fudge

parts.note: muck is dung
when time's up, it is all over

explanation.surface: Something awful smeared over a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Fudge looks like the sweet; it is the verb meaning to botch.
explanation.definitionFit: To fudge a job is to bungle it, so the verb phrase for botching fits.

clue.text: Monica extremely taken aback by President's surprise move?

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the kept letters are read in reverse
extremely means only the extremities, the two end letters, are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
George W Bush, the US President

explanation.surface: Monica Lewinsky shocked by a presidential advance, though it was Clinton, not Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Monica Lewinsky scandal; the apostrophe-s of President's is the link 's being dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from a hidden position.

clue.text: Throw up over stout-'earted type's jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: to lob is to throw

indicators.note: the apostrophe shows a Cockney dropped aitch, so the H goes

parts.note: a stout-hearted type is a brave one

explanation.surface: Someone vomits over a fat person's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like vomiting, and 'stout' like fat; in a down clue, over means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket ending above the waist.

clue.text: European city responsible for personal problem: getting stuffed by a load of sailors

indicators.note: something stuffed has filling pushed inside it

parts.note: body odour, a personal hygiene problem
the Royal Navy, the British fleet

explanation.surface: A rude joke about a city where someone's problem is being had by a crowd of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is body odour; RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brno is the second city of the Czech Republic, in central Europe.

clue.text: see 10ac.
see 6dn.
Maude taking top off — without pressure, breast bent

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
removing the top of a word means its first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its first letter
P is the symbol for pressure
slang for a breast

explanation.surface: A woman named Maude strips off her top, revealing a crooked breast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like describing the breast, but it is the definition: a talent or inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is a natural talent for it, just as an aptitude is.

clue.text: Road construction and sex expert

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so the letters are assembled anew

parts.note: taken as written
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A list of jobs: roadworks, and sex therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex expert' reads as one phrase, but expert alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and dexterous, an adjectival sense of expert.
